#4204. 2027 Video Game Grammy Nominations Include Avatar: Frontiers Of Pandora For The Third Time

Since 2023, the Recording Academy has included an official category for video game soundtracks, adding an air of legitimacy to a diverse musical medium we know and love. Today, we learned the list of nominees for the 2027 Grammy ceremony, and it's an interesting lineup. The nominations are as follows:

As is often the case, what stands out most about these nominees is how, generally speaking, they don't fully align with gaming culture's favorite soundtracks of the year, and instead often trend toward the most recognizable IP (often franchises with films) of the year. On that note, it's most surprising to see that Avatar: Frontiers of Pandora has been nominated for the third year in a row: once for the base game, once for the Secrets of the Spires DLC, and now for the From The Ashes DLC. None of these soundtracks are bad by any means, but their Grammy representation far outweighs their cultural footprint.

The standout here is Ghost of Yōtei, which is not an adaptation of the massive franchises the other games fall into. However, it's also a Sony-published game, which have a pretty good track record of getting nominations, potentially due to the company's massive presence in the music and film industries. Still, Ghost of Yōtei has a great, unique score that's deserving of its spot, and also one previously nominated for best music at the 2025 Game Awards. The Grammys accept any releases between October 1 of one year and September 30 of the following year, so Ghost of Yōtei barely made the cut for this window. The Game Awards nominees will be announced tomorrow – it will be interesting to see how much overlap there is between the categories.

This batch of Grammy noms also has fewer recurring nominees than past years. This is Gordy Haab's third nomination (he won in 2024 for Star Wars Jedi: Survivor) and John Paesano's second nomination (he was nominated in 2025 for Marvel's Spider-Man 2). It's also the first year since the awards' creation without Bear McCreary or Austin Wintory nominations.

Last year's nominations left a sour taste in the mouths of many, with several DLC nominees and a complete lack of Clair Obscur: Expedition 33, the year's standout hit that many specifically praised for its music. This year certainly has snubs (Mewgenics, Fire Emblem: Fortune's Weave, and Control Resonant all come to mind), but none as egregious as last year.

What do you think was the best video game score from the last year? Let us know in the comments!

#4200. Make Room For GTAVI By Deleting Your PS5 Trophy Clips

Hard drive space is a premium commodity, and its value has never been more apparent than in the approximately two and a half days leading up to the launch of Grand Theft Auto VI. The game is a whopping 209 GB, but thankfully you can purchase the game and preload it now – which you should do because who knows if the servers are going to be able to handle the strain of what is officially the most pre-ordered game ever on both PlayStation and Xbox platforms.

The easy (and likely necessary) answer is to delete the big games you aren't currently playing off your hard drive, but there is a cache of arguably unnecessary data on PlayStation 5 that might get you there before you have to make hard decisions.

You may have turned it off (Settings > Capture and Broadcasts > Captures > Trophies under the Auto-captures section > Save Trophy Videos under the Video Clips section > Change to None), which if that is the case, then I'm sorry. I can't help you. But the default setting which maybe you've never touched, is saving a lot of unnecessary video.

Every time you get a Trophy on PlayStation 5, it creates a short video clip that I bet you never have and never will watch. Here's how to delete all those videos fairly quickly to free up at least some space.

First up, go to the Media Gallery. The quickest way to do that is to press the screenshot button to the left of the touchpad, tap over to the most recent media capture on the left, press X, and then press the Go to Media Gallery button.

Next, go to the Trophies tab, go to the Sort and Filter option (the downward arrow with the three lines), and change Media Type to Video Clips.

After that, go back a few screens and go to the Select Multiple option (the overlapping squares with the check mark on it). Go ahead and press the Select All option, then press Delete, and then hold your breath and commit by pressing Delete again.

In taking screenshots to write this little article, I deleted 110 14-second clips. That's about 25 minutes of video footage, which ain't nothing. Maybe it will help you not delete that one game that you started three years ago that you are definitely going to get back to any day now.

#4199. The Most Loved and Hated JRPGs by Fans

Murillo Zerbinatto is a JRPG enthusiast, writer, and editor. He has played over 300 RPGs during his gaming career, with 90% of them being JRPGs.

JRPGs have long since become a distinct phenomenon as a specific subgenre of RPGs, even when they are not produced in Japan. Fixed characters, linear narratives, creative progression, and an atduesthetic usually inspired by anime are what tell us at a glance what makes a JRPG stand apart from any other subgenre under the role-playing umbrella. And to be honest, those exact elements are what draw me to the genre, sometimes removing one or adding another.

Global media is warming up to JRPGs, yet several standout titles still get snubbed at The Game Awards.

However, while there is a slightly more civilized consensus around what makes the best fighting game or racing game, the JRPGs fanbase always seems deeply divided. Some titles seem to sit at the same level of love and hate for fans, no matter which side you're on. That is why I decided to talk today about the most loved and most hated JRPGs by the public. This isn't a consensus or an objective truth, but a fun look at what I have observed after years on forums, debating with fellow JRPG lovers, and tracking the fanbase's overall perception.

I will alternate between hated and loved entries and avoid repeating franchises to keep the list dynamic.

While I couldn't find a direct primary source confirming this claim, outlets like Kotaku and RPGFan say the same thing: due to Xenosaga Episode II flopping so hard, the series was cut from its intended six episodes to just three. For fans hoping to see Tetsuya Takahashi's vision fully realized, that was a massive blow and certainly left a mark of hatred on the second Xenosaga.

While Xenosaga Episode I: Der Wille zur Macht went over budget and featured far more cinematics than the average JRPG player was accustomed to (yeap), it was still a satisfactory experience. The second one? Not so much. The shift in art direction and the battle system genuinely pushed players away and, allegedly, led Bandai Namco to safeguard its investment by wrapping up the entire story as a trilogy. Much like Xenogears, Xenosaga became a beautiful what-could-have-been scenario, though luckily we eventually got to see Takahashi's ambitions realized with Xenoblade, which is still going strong.

To be completely honest, I am not that big of a fan of EarthBound. I played EarthBound Beginnings, also known as Mother, and found it impressive for an NES JRPG. Shortly after, I moved on to EarthBound, which I had played a long time ago and didn't remember much, and I walked away unimpressed. Maybe the American parody didn't resonate with me (I am not American), or maybe I played it too late, and the cultural zeitgeist didn't hit me the same way.

Even so, I fully recognize how much people who enjoy this JRPG truly adore it. They spare no praise, speak fondly of the experience, and admire not only the game itself, but also its creator, Shigesato Itoi. Many of those fans claim Mother 3, a title that never officially left Japan, is even better, but since I didn't vibe with the second entry, I have little interest in trying it.

Sometimes a game is hated for its themes, other times for an overly boring battle system, or perhaps because of an obnoxious character we cannot stand looking at. Occasionally, however, games draw hatred simply for feeling apathetic, failing to spark any real emotion in the player, and offering nothing particularly remarkable. That's exactly the case with Tales of Zestiria for many Tales fans.

Mind you, I actually enjoy the game, and it was the very first Tales of title where I earned the platinum trophy. I was never overly critical of Sorey's journey, the complex equipment fusion system, or even the misleading marketing around Alisha's protagonism. I mean, okay, fair enough, those all sound like completely valid points of criticism, yet I still had a good time. Not everyone can say the same, and whenever you look at a Tales of tier list, Zestiria almost always sits right at the bottom.

Apparently, there are two types of fans in the JRPG world: those who love Suikoden II and those who haven't played it yet. I am not kidding here. I considered adding Xenogears to this spot because I know it has a very vocal fanbase, quite scary to be honest, borderline toxic. But Suikoden? That feels like a genuine relationship, a true love situation. Every time you meet someone who says Suikoden II is their favorite game, you can practically see their eyes light up.

To a large extent, I get it! Suikoden II is awesome. The grounded political plot stood out at a time when countless games were mostly about slaying God in a high fantasy setting. The 108 recruitable characters, each carrying their own motivation and reason for joining the resistance. The six-party-member battles with combo skills, and so on. Okay, you might need to use a walkthrough to recruit everyone and unlock the true ending, but the journey itself is already wonderful, and Luca Blight is a terrific villain. What is there not to love, right? Glory to Suikoden.

Some JRPG mechanics from the golden age deserve a second wind in modern titles.

There is nothing more miserable than watching a series you love, follow closely, and appreciate in every detail slowly fall from grace. For me, that didn't happen with Star Ocean, because I genuinely love Star Ocean: The Divine Force, though that is precisely how many felt after Star Ocean: Till the End of Time, the third entry. Plenty of fans didn't care for Star Ocean: The Last Hope yet could still stomach it, but Star Ocean: Integrity and Faithlessness? Just mentioning the name makes me feel your glare.

The fifth Star Ocean suffered from an affliction that hit many JRPG franchises during that era: constricting budgets. I know that doesn't excuse its final quality, but it is the reality. The game severely lacked traditional cutscenes, playing out almost entirely through real-time in-engine camera angles, not out of artistic charm, but due to a lack of investment. I still like the game for two reasons: Item Creation remains incredible, and as someone who loves constantly swapping between party members, being able to deploy everyone into battle at once was a blast, even if having seven party members acting simultaneously got confusing and felt like a bit too much. It had a chaotic family reunion vibe, you know.

Out of all the JRPG fans I know, well over half say they discovered or fell in love with the genre after playing Final Fantasy VII. That fact alone could summarize this entire entry, because you either know someone just like that or you are that person yourself. I am a bit older, so I played other JRPGs before FFVII, though my cousin fits that exact mold, since he still uses an email address with the game's acronym in his handle to this day.

It is completely understandable, mind you. Final Fantasy VII was a global phenomenon that paved the way for JRPGs to gain worldwide recognition. That is why if you watch footage from the E3 showcase where the remake was unveiled, you will see countless explosive reactions. I know many newcomers to the genre or franchise don't understand why Square Enix split the remake into three parts, calling the company mercenary (fitting for the game's plot, to be honest). Yet, I believe Square did it to honor the franchise's legacy, deliver something fresh for longtime fans, and naturally attract a new audience who can experience that same magic veterans felt when they first played and fell in love with it.

Whereas with most entries I listed as most hated (not hated by me, remember!) I tried to soften the blow and use euphemisms to avoid insulting people who enjoy those games or the developers behind them. For Lunar: Dragon Song, though, the gloves are completely off. I had only heard rumors about it, about how this mechanic was terrible and that feature was lousy, until one day I decided to test it for myself.

Good lord, it is awful. So many baffling design decisions make me genuinely wonder how anyone let them pass. First, and most obviously, simply running in the game drains your HP. I mean, what? Then there are two separate reward modes per battle, one granting only experience points and another granting only loot. I didn't understand that system at first and left loot mode active, feeling bizarrely weak despite fighting endless battles. On top of that, combat has mandatory auto-targeting, plus a bland story, forgettable characters, and other uninspiring features. Lunar: Dragon Song is universally hated, and it deserves every bit of it.

Whenever someone asks me which JRPG I would recommend to a complete newcomer to the genre, the answer nine times out of ten is Chrono Trigger. Pointing to a 1995 release even today speaks volumes about the work's enduring relevance and timelessness. And I will go a step further: that recommendation doesn't rely on cheap nostalgia alone, because Chrono Trigger truly is a spectacle, with pacing, gameplay, and design that can captivate even the most stubborn skeptics who resist JRPGs.

And of course, among JRPG enthusiasts, it is tough to find anyone who doesn't genuinely love Chrono Trigger. You might have critiques about it (I certainly do), or complain about one small detail or another. Still, it's nearly impossible to deny that it is a masterpiece and a majestic blueprint for building a JRPG. It stands undeniably as the most beloved JRPG of all time, even if you don't happen to be one of the people who love it.

These JRPGs still remain on the Game Boy, just waiting to take us on surprisingly deep adventures.

#4198. Starsand Island is a life and farming sim that isn't gacha, and it's out next week

Starsand Island officially has an Early Access release date, and it sounds like it won't stay there for years.

Though it may seem like we just had a big life sim release in Heartopia, 2026 actually has more than one highly-anticipated release in that particular subgenre of cozy game. The next big one on the horizon is Starsand Island, the life and farming sim from Seed Sparkle Lab.

The game has been gaining momentum since the launch of a demo in October last year, but the developer never quite managed to commit to a date for its debut title. Until now.

Seed Sparkle Lab announced today that Starsand Island will enter Early Access on February 11, which is only a bit over one week from now. This goes for Steam and the Xbox Preview Program version.

The developer said to expect a fairly short Early Access run, as the full launch is expected in the summer of this year. When the full release arrives, the game will also make the jump to PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series, as well as Switch 2.

The full release is also expected to bring Steam Deck support and introduce the multiplayer mode, which will not be available during Early Access

Starsand Island has something of a unique look compared to other games in the subgenre. The storybook, anime-inspired aesthetics are popular in the realm of gacha games, of course. However, seeing as this particular game isn’t gacha, being a premium product means it’s going to offer something free-to-play games aren’t designed to.

Speaking of which, the game will be available in two editions: Standard and Deluxe, with the latter including Romanticism-inspired outfits, furniture, and other customisation items. If you buy either during launch, you’ll also get a Chinese New Year bonus with even more outfits and furniture.

On top of the usual systems of farming, mining, and making friends with adorable characters (and animals), the game also has combat that pits you against ancient guardians. You can, of course, also build a home in it, and decorate it to your heart's content.

Seed Sparkle Lab says you can expect about 100 hours of content in the Early Access launch build, and more features will arrive over the course of the next six or so months, including a crossover event with My Time At Portia.

You can look forward to more Starsand Island coverage from us in the near future. Until then, you can get started by planning who you’re going to date now.

#4195. Nioh 3 launches, immediately becomes the most played Nioh ever on Steam

Just a few hours after launch, Nioh 3 is already the biggest release in series history on Steam.

It sounds like Koei Tecmo’s decision to finally release a Nioh game on PC day-and-date with PlayStation has paid off. The highly-anticipated Nioh 3 has gone live across both platforms, a first for a series that typically spends its initial release months as a console exclusive.

On Steam, and despite having only been available for just a few hours, the game has broken series records, and it continues to climb.

At the time of writing, Nioh 3 has peaked at 42,822 concurrent players on Steam (via SteamDB), and the number keeps going up. Because it’s in the middle of day in Europe and everyone is at work, it’s entirely possible - if not likely - that this figure will get much higher. A weekend bump is also possible, as we’ve seen with several recent releases.

As it stands, the current peak concurrent is enough to get the game in Steam’s top 20 most played games.

This already puts it ahead of all other Nioh games on Steam. The original Nioh peaked at 10,649 when it released in November, 2017. Nioh 2 fared much better, peaking at 41,325 concurrent players in February, 2021.

Of course, you could see that success coming a mile away. The game is currently number one worldwide in Steam’s list of top sellers. This is a jump of 46 positions, for a total of three weeks Nioh 3 has spent in that list.

There are many reasons as to why Nioh 3 has done as well as it has. Word of mouth coming off last year’s PS5-exclusive demo, and the more positive coverage that followed since are just two.

Just last week, Team Ninja released a pretty generous demo across both platforms, which has been well received by players, and likely contributed to sales, in no small part because progress in the demo carries over to the full game.

Critical reviews have been incredibly positive, too. We awarded the game four out of five stars, calling it “Team Ninja’s most accomplished action game, and the series’ most accessible.” It will be interesting to see what number the highest peak concurrent actually settles on over the weekend.

Until then, if you’re jumping in yourself, our Nioh 3 guides are essential reading. Start off with these useful and actually informative gameplay tips, and don’t start playing until you’ve changed these settings. #4193. GodLike Esports sweep Trigger Point Esports to stay unbeaten in South Asia Kickoff qualifier

GodLike Esports beat Trigger Point Esports 2-0 in the upper bracket of the VCT Pacific Kickoff South Asia qualifier. Only two South Asian sides will reach the Last Chance Qualifier, where a single place at Kickoff in Bangkok is on offer.

GodLike Esports opened their VCT Pacific Kickoff: South Asia – Qualifier 2027 playoff campaign with a 2-0 win over Trigger Point Esports on Monday 23 November 2026. GodLike took both maps of the best-of-three upper bracket quarter-final. Trigger Point Esports now drop into the lower bracket of the double-elimination format.

The playoffs are being held online by Riot Games and JioBLAST. Series in the bracket are played as best-of-three or best-of-five.

GodLike arrived in form. They reached the playoffs with an unbeaten 4-0 record in the open qualifier, VLR.gg reported. They shared joint first to fourth place in that event, which ran from 17 to 20 November. Trigger Point finished in the group placed fifth to eighth.

GodLike fielded Karam1L, Paradox and RvK from India, alongside sayoo from Indonesia and azyshaha from the Philippines. Sabyasachi ‘Antidote’ Bose is listed as head coach, with Samar as substitute. Trigger Point’s listed players are SangraM, WEELJACK and RaJ.

South Asian teams cannot qualify directly for Kickoff. The top two from the playoffs join the Oceania playoff winner and the Southeast Asia playoff runner-up in a four-team Last Chance Qualifier. Only its winner goes through to Kickoff in Bangkok, according to Dot Esports.

The stakes are high. Twelve teams will play at Kickoff, and the top three will qualify for Masters 1. The route stays narrow later in the season too. South Asia has no direct place at the Cups, with Cup 1 in Manila and Cup 2 in Tokyo. It sends two teams to an eight-team Pacific LCQ, and the winner takes the last Cup place.

The qualifier also has a new organiser. Riot picked JioBLAST to run the South Asia qualifiers instead of NODWIN Gaming, the previous organiser. Riot has not said why it made the change.

The UK interest lies with SIGN Esports. They beat Zexar Esports 2-0 in another upper bracket quarter-final. Russel ‘Russ’ Mendes joined SIGN Esports on 16 November 2026. He is the only player from the UK in the eight-team playoff field.

Russ was born in 1998 and is of Indian descent. He won the VALORANT Challengers 2025 South Asia Grand Final with Velocity Gaming on 13 July 2025, when they beat S8UL 3-1.

GodLike Esports and SIGN Esports both remain in the upper bracket, one defeat away from the lower bracket. Trigger Point Esports and Zexar Esports must win from the lower bracket to stay in contention for a top-two finish. The playoffs run until 29 November 2026.

#4191. Honkai: Star Rail Version 4.0 brings a new world, and a Fortnite collaboration

Honkai: Star Rail's next major update introduces a whole new planet to the RPG, and way more besides.

HoYoverse just wrapped up a big Honkai: Star Rail Special Program. We’ve been waiting for this one for a couple of weeks now thanks to a delay, but the developer has finally delivered all the news on Version 4.0, which will arrive February 13.

The upcoming major release is dubbed No Aha at Full Moon for a very good reason. Aha's Planarcadia is the big new world headlining Version 4.0.

Planarcadia is a place whose description sounds a bit like a Warhammer 40,000 Eldar homeworld, and is quite open about its cyberpunk inspirations. In-universe, however, it was born out of the pages of an art canvas, and it’s a world where pleasure is king.

The squad’s host in this chapter is Madam Pearl, who will oversee the the Astral Express’ return to the place where they first began their journey. Duomension City is where you’re going to land, and meet the creatures that dwell in this world.

The imagenae of Planarcadia require attention to survive, and they feed off people’s Wishpower. If they don’t get any attention, they perish, which does tie into the general themes of the place. Duomension City has other interesting locations that you’re going to visit, such as the Graphia Academy art school, the commercial district of Dovebrook, and a few other places hidden behind mysterious entrances.

The Phantasmoon Games is another highlight of Planarcadia, a competitive spectacle where you’ll have a chance to compete to become Aeon for a Minute. If you make it to the final stages, you may earn an audience with The Laughter.

Much like the world where the games take place, the whole point of the competition is to attract the most attention, so rules are a bit loose as to how you manage to do that. The event will bring together several of the game’s factions, though not everyone is there for the competition.

As you explore Planarcadia, if you have characters on your team who are on the newly-playable Path of Elation, you’ll earn Punchlines. The more you accumulate, the closer you get to catching Aha’s attention, which triggers Aha Instant.

Version 4.0 introduces two new 5-Star characters to Honkai: Star Rail. General Yao Guang (Madam Yao) is one, a Seer Strategist from the Xianzhou Alliance's Yuque. If you’ve been playing the game, you may already be familiar with her voice, as she's previously been in touch with our heroes via radio link. But V4.0 marks her first on-screen appearance, as well as her playable debut.

General Yao Guang is a Physical character on the Path of Elation whose specialty is using Weal and Woe Lots in battle, which she uses to increase Elation for allies, and grant everyone Punchline any time she uses a Skill. If an Aha Instant is triggered, she casts Woe Lots, which debuff enemies, causing them to take increased damage, all while regenerating Skill Points for the rest of the team.

Her aptly named Certified Banger buff adds one extra instance of Elation to teammates’ attacks. And her Ultimate grants the team Punchline, and triggers an extra Aha Instant.

The other new arrival is likewise a Path of Elation devotee. Sparxie is a suspiciously familiar streamer who uses her influencer skills in combat. When she fights, she turns the fight into a battle for attention, as she forces enemies to engage in a race for upvotes.

When you consume Skill Points, Sparxie will get gifts, which in turn cause her to regenerate Skill Points and Punchlines for the team. You can continue doing this to increase your damage. When Aha Instant is triggered, Sparxie unleashes a lucky draw that deals damage to enemies with each bounce.

She also benefits from the Certified Banger state, which causes the gifs she receives to deal more Elation damage to a random enemy target. Her Ultimate also deals more Elation damage.

Version 4.0 will see a few re-runs, too. Black Swan, Evernight, and Hysilens will be part of the first half's Warp events. The second half will see the return of Sparkle, Cerydra, and Rappa — that's right, HoYoverse have finally remembered Rappa exists, after one of the longest rerun waits in the game's history! Both Black Swan and Sparkle are getting a few tweaks to their kit with this version, too, so the timing works.

If you log in after launch, you’ll get 20 free pulls and a new free outfit for Ruan Mei. If you play while the Yao Guang fortune event is active, you could earn 1,600 Stellar Jades. You can also expect a free 5-Star character selector to arrive at some point after launch, giving you a free choice between popular (but admittedly a bit old for the meta these days) limited-banner characters Jing Yuan, Kafka, Dan Heng • Imbibitor Lunae, Jingliu, Sparkle, Acheron, and Aventurine.

Finally, the other major news is a Fortnite collaboration. Starting February 26, Kafka and Blade will join Epic’s battle royale shooter. On that day, you’ll find skins of the two Stellaron Hunters in the Fortnite Item Shop, and the new outfits are even compatible with Fortnite's LEGO styles. You can also expect other customisation bits like Back Bling, Pickaxe, and more to be part of the package.

If you download the game on the Epic Games Store, and take part in Honkai: Star Rail-themed activities, you’ll also get the Blade character outfit in Fortnite for free. Event schedule and timing will be announced at a later date.

#4190. Ubisoft Claims It Encourages, But Doesn’t Require Generative AI Usage During Game Development

Patrick Souza is a writer for DualShockers who has been writing for over 5 years, specializing in JRPGs, roguelikes, and other genres such as MMOs. He previously worked for Prima Games, The Escapist, and The Gamer, and holds a degree in Journalism.

As AI usage during game development and discussions surrounding it become more prominent, Ubisoft has been taking a firm stance on embracing it. But according to the company itself, the usage of such tools is more like a suggestion than a rule to be strictly followed.

According to a report yesterday from Vertical Slice, the company has been enforcing generative AI usage across its development teams in order to increase productivity and enhance the project in general. And if you choose not to implement it, you would have to justify your choice.

Nintendo has filed multiple patents that have opened the door for DS, 3DS, and Wii U games to arrive on the Switch 2, all for the low low price of owning two consoles.

However, Ubisoft has now responded to the original reporting, stating that while they do encourage AI usage across all production stages, it doesn’t mean that they require every single project to implement it, as they still need to be added only when it actually makes sense.

The original version of Vertical Slice’s report states that, after speaking with various employees (who chose to remain anonymous due to possible backlash), Ubisoft is looking forward to increasing its gen-AI usage across all titles. If they choose not to use it, they have to detail the reasons for their choice. Otherwise, their ideas wouldn’t be approved to be worked on.

The report came out days after Ubisoft announced that their newest studio, Motherbrain, would be an AI-focused studio, being an important part of their “new operating model”. The announcement also came days after over 160 staff members were let go from their positions in Canada-based studios.

According to Ubisoft, they are simply encouraging their “teams to explore where AI can be useful and bring value to their work.”

While it all seems daunting and terrifying, the studio decided to step up to clarify exactly what it all means. According to Ubisoft, they are simply encouraging their “teams to explore where AI can be useful and bring value to their work,” and ensuring that no employee is being silently forced to implement gen-AI in their work.This aligns with a claim from one of the employees Vertical Slice spoke with. According to them, while they aren’t outright mandated to use AI in their projects, the company has fully decided to implement it whenever they have the chance.

While "AI psychosis" has been a thing for a while, it’s undeniable that the existence of generative tools has greatly shifted the industry and its inner workings in just a couple of years. From waves of layoffs followed by AI-pilled initiatives and the implementation of disclaimers about its usage on official game store pages, it’s hard not to be alarmed by all of these signals.

Ubisoft has been a huge player in these changes. The new Motherbrain studio is a byproduct of Teammates, an AI experiment from last year. This AI-powered demo uses the tool to mold your experience according to your voice and actions, as NPCs will react to your commands and, as stated on their official site, “allow players to experience the story in their own way”.

With all of these new advances in mind, it’s not unexpected to see such a posture from the company. However, it doesn’t mean they should be free of criticism when it's due. It’s hard not to associate all of the previously mentioned layoffs (which have been ever more common in the industry) with the increasing fear of being replaced by AI.

Another Ubisoft employee also mentioned feeling “cornered by generative AI all the time” since the recent attitude shift from the higher-ups, implying that some pressure over AI usage does exist inside the company.

This doesn’t mean that Ubisoft’s own statement is incorrect. It could simply be a different way of perceiving attitudes and decisions taken by the company. But with so many AI-related incidents across the industry, such as the recent wave of AI game copies, it’s hard not to be worried about the future of gaming.

#4187. The Blood Of Dawnwalker Just Got A Free 1.2 Update, Adding New Game Plus

The Blood of Dawnwalker is one of the year's biggest, most ambitious games, and the developers over at Rebel Wolves have done a good job cleaning up bugs and performance issues in the weeks since launch. Today, that trend continued; the new 1.2 update is out now on PS5, Xbox Series X/S, and PC, and it adds New Game Plus.

The new mode is uniquely ideal for a game like Dawnwalker. The narrative is very player-driven, whether it has to do with your literal dialogue options, your ability to manage your vampiric hunger, or the order you complete quests, and all of these elements can cause your experience to vary wildly. It makes sense, then, that players would want to jump back in to try things again and see what might happen if the game is played differently, and New Game Plus allows them to do that while keeping combat fresh.

According to the update notes on the Dawnwalker website, "NG+ unlocks after you complete the game’s Epilogue and lets you experience the story again while keeping your progress – mainly your character level, skills, and inventory." You don't gain access to these skills until you complete the prologue, however, which marks the adventure's proper start.

The new mode will also rebalance the world's level scaling. In the base game, certain areas are much harder than others, but in New Game Plus, all enemies will rise in power to match your level, meaning you can explore the world in whatever order you want. On that note, the level cap has also been raised to 100, and protagonist Coen can collect new, more powerful versions of weapons marked with an "NG+" label.

That's basically everything in this update. Rebel Wolves also added some slight tweaks to combat in the base game and adjusted some geometry in the open world, but the main focus here was New Game Plus. This is in contrast to the 1.1 update, which added a much wider suite of bug fixes and made the game run more smoothly.

#4182. GTA 6 Developer Reveals Why He Voted Against Union

Michael Manning (He/Him) has been enamored with video games since he first played the Sonic Classic Collection as a child. With decades of experience in gaming and a full tour as a Gaming Journalist, Michael is ready to step up to the plate. From AAA to the smallest passion projects, his motto is that every piece of ar

When you’re making a big budget video game, it's likely different members of staff and development teams are going to clash. Be it creative differences, long-term team structure, or even post-project follow-through, no unit is a legion, and these split opinions can easily shape not only the title itself, but the future of everyone who worked on it.

GTA 6 has mountains of references, including unique cosmetics! Let's take a look at how to find some plumber-worthy apparel.

Rockstar has faced public inquiries into the health of its developers over the monumental Grand Theft Auto 6, and union rumors have floated for weeks. With the vote finally coming through rejecting the recognition of said union, one staff member, named Thomas March, came out to explain why he thinks the team is better off without it, at least for now.

Discussion of the union representing Rockstar staff has been a rumor mill for weeks, with no clear answer about what's happening behind the scenes. Following an internal vote handled by a third party, Rockstar staff voted not to establish the IWGB as their union of choice, while maintaining the option to establish a union of their own at a later date.

In a post clarifying exactly what went down behind the scenes, Thomas March, an associate principal developer at Rockstar, described the IWGB’s position on Rockstar staff’s treatment as “endlessly frustrating…”. To March, the Independent Workers’ Union of Great Britain represented a bottleneck in staff voices, stopping individuals from arguing for their own benefits individually.

According to March, Rockstar’s worker treatment is nothing short of industry-leading. “Nowhere else have I been listened to so closely, treated with such respect, even while working with veterans and experts bar none.” Thomas claims that Rockstar’s treatment of each individual staff member means that formal recognition of a union isn’t really necessary.

When you’re making a big budget video game, it's likely different members of staff and development teams are going to clash.

Between flexible hours, employee benefits, and a truly caring workplace, March paints Rockstar as the fledgling developer’s dream, all the while decrying other staff members who raised complaints over crunch and questionable conditions of their own.

Rockstar staff does have its own internal union, dubbed the RSGWU, but the IWGB would have granted the staff unprecedented protections and argumentative power. While March cited the independence as a major boon, unions only get results when a staff force is unified. For now, they’ll have to make do with the RSGWU, a decent union that seems to have granted the team their own voice amongst investors.

The general response to March’s defense of the vote has been less than glowing, with dozens of fellow devs and union members decrying the result as short-sighted and selfish. Amidst the clapbacks and dismissals are former coworkers and industry peers lamenting a squandered chance, describing their own negative experiences with Rockstar’s internal face.

At the end of the day, each and every person can only share their individual experiences, each of which will paint their biases in a major deciding vote like Rockstar’s. The nature of the vote means that, should conditions fail to improve for everyone, members of Rockstar staff can try to recognize another union, or empower their current union to fight for their rights more actively.

Whether you believe Rockstar is a bastion of developer health or a corporate machine aiming for quality over all else, at current each individual member of Rockstar staff will need to choose.

Independent negotiations or small-scale union building is all they have at present, and while the recognition of the IWGB in such a prestigious studio could have made major waves, every individual is sure to vote for their own future.

The third upper-bracket quarter-final of the VCT Pacific Kickoff: South Asia – Qualifier 2027 needed a deciding third map.

Sunset ran for 51 minutes. Revenant XSpark levelled by winning Haven 13-5 in 35 minutes. They then won the deciding map, which lasted 49 minutes.

The scoreline matches the two sides’ Predator League India semi-final, which Revenant XSpark also won 2-1. GOC lost the third-place match of that event to GodLike Esports. GOC now drop into the lower bracket and face RANKERS in the first lower round on Wednesday 25 November.

Kryon booked their place in the upper semi-final by beating RANKERS 2-1. On the other side of the upper bracket, GodLike Esports beat Trigger Point Esports 2-0 and SIGN Esports beat Zexar Esports by the same score.

Second place in that Predator League event earned Kryon 125,000 INR, while the winners collected 250,000 INR, VLR.gg reported. Both teams qualified for the APAC Predator League 2027, an offline event in Ho Chi Minh City.

Revenant XSpark played the Predator League with Lightningfast, hellff, Hoax, deecee and Venka. Rinsat, now listed on Revenant XSpark’s roster alongside Hoax, Techno, venka, k1ngkappa and Madelyn, appeared in Kryon’s lineup for that event.

Riot Games and JioBLAST are running the playoffs online as an eight-team double-elimination bracket from 23 to 29 November. The field came through an online Open Qualifier of 152 teams, held from 17 to 20 November. Revenant XSpark finished in the top four there, while GOC placed in the 5th–8th group.

The South Asian qualifiers will be joined at the Last Chance Qualifier by one team from Oceania and the runner-up of the SEA Kickoff Playoffs. ONE Up is organising that event with Riot Games.

#4177. Civilization Developer Firaxis Lays Off A Third Of Its Staff

Firaxis, the studio behind the Civilization series, has laid off around 60 employees, representing a third of its staff. The report comes from Bloomberg’s Jason Schreier.

In a statement provided to Bloomberg by a spokesperson from 2K, a subsidiary of Firaxis' owner, Take-Two, “Firaxis is restructuring and recentering around the studio’s core strength—designing world class strategy games that have set the industry standard for the genre for the last 30 years. As part of these changes, the size of the studio is being reduced to focus on design, technology and the player experience, which means saying goodbye to talented colleagues who helped build Firaxis. These decisions are never easy, but they’re essential to build the next chapter of Firaxis.”

In addition to the 60 affected staffers, Firaxis studio head Heather Hazen is also departing. Bloomberg also reports, via anonymous Firaxis employees speaking to the outlet, that the studio is working on an unannounced XCOM game that has had a challenging development, with the team recently missing an important development milestone. This project, if it releases, will be the first Firaxis-developed XCOM game since XCOM: Chimera Squad in 2020.

Firaxis’ most recent release is Civilization VII, which launched in February 2025 to favorable reviews but initially "slow" sales, according to Take-Two CEO Strauss Zelnick last August.  The game currently has a Mixed reception on Steam after Firaxis spent the last year updating the game to address player complaints. Before Civilization VII, Firaxis shipped Marvel's Midnight Suns in 2022, another critically well-received game that failed to meet sales expectations.

#4175. Battlefield 6's next season will speed up battle pass progression, and make it so Redsec players who don't own the game can actually make progress

Season 2 of Battlefield 6 looks to bring a host of broad, positive changes to XP, progression, audio and more.

Ahead of the start of Battlefield 6’s Season 2 next week, Battlefield Studios has shared some insight into a few of the major goals the developer has with the Season 2 patch. The game’s second season was delayed in mid-January, and the developer even brought back Battlefield Labs to test out some of the new content and features coming with the new season.

Indeed, the broader goals BF Studios shared with players in a new blog post reflect some of what Labs players already went hands-on with, while others are the result of work on long-standing issues with both the game itself, as well as free-to-play mode Redsec.

We know that Season 2 is introducing a big new map to the game, Contaminated, which the developer has been teasing. The map will indeed arrive in the first part of the season, and it’s going to do so alongside a new LTM that “introduces a new element of tactics.” A second, “high-intensity map” will debut later into the season, alongside another LTM where players battle through an underground base, in darkness.

The real meat of the blog post, however, covers the broader gameplay changes everyone will see once the new season kicks off. There’s a massive focus on player progression, especially when it concerns free-to-play Redsec players.

Challenges are being streamlined yet again, with more broad parameters that don’t require specific modes. Some, like dailies, will also allow for assists to count towards their criteria. Less restrictive challenges are welcome, but even more so is the faster battle pass progression.

BF Studios is changing the rate at which battle pass Tokens are earned from career XP, and making it so they’re earnable by playing the game normally, and by completing weekly challenges. These changes should also help Redsec players, who will also benefit from faster career and weapon XP earn rates - across both battle royale, and Gauntlet. In general, the career experience should feel more rewarding, especially for earlier ranks.

Weapon balance and recoil are two areas that will continue to evolve in Battlefield 6, it seems, and Season 2 is specifically tackling recoil patterns to make them more consistent when you compensate for them.

Movement is being adjusted with the Season 2 patch, too, though thankfully it’s limited to general feel that touches areas like vaulting, ladder transitions, and acceleration curves. You should also see better continuity and consistency between animations and feel.

Audio is getting a pass with the upcoming patch, especially when it comes to footstep and interaction audio. This also extends to something the developer has been working on improving for a while, and it has to do with how the game decides which audio tracks to prioritise in busy situations.

Tomorrow, the full Battlefield 6 Season 2 trailer will be released, while a more detailed roadmap is expected by the end of this week.

#4174. 7 Details That Make GTA 6 A Flawed Game

Ronald is a video game journalist with more than 10 years of experience in the industry, working on several of the most important Spanish websites.

GTA 6 has become the highest-rated video game of all time according to Metacritic, sparking debate about whether it truly represents the closest thing to perfection in our history.

As someone who has enjoyed the series since the century's beginning, and who considers himself a huge fan of the Red Dead Redemption franchise, I have mixed feelings about this assertion, as the game's shortcomings are not hidden at any point.

Do these weaknesses diminish its revolutionary and utterly awe-inspiring nature? Not in the slightest, as it remains an extraordinary adventure that we will admire for decades, even with its imperfections.

Therefore, in order to discuss the game honestly and respectfully while also questioning the merits of its unparalleled achievements, here are seven details that make GTA 6 a flawed game.

Considering its draw distance, countless interactive elements, and dynamic entities that come alive in Leonida every second you walk, it's completely understandable that GTA 6 doesn't have a consistent frame rate.

Although this might say more about the platforms it was released on than the product itself, it certainly impacts the overall experience, especially in the most spectacular sequences where so many factors converge that the game seems on the verge of crashing.

As someone who grew up with such limited hardware that I had to play Hollow Knight at 15 FPS, I'd be lying if I said it was a negative aspect that bothered me too much, yet its easy and regularly noticeable nature is equally undeniable.

When the next-gen and PC versions arrive, I'm sure I'll have to update the article and remove this entry, but for now, it's the first drawback you notice, and it's impossible to ignore.

Striking the right pace for an open-world game's main story is among the most difficult tasks in the entire genre, as the chances of the player getting stuck, overwhelmed, or impatient are extremely high.

For better or worse, GTA 6 exposes itself to these pitfalls by presenting a campaign whose problem isn't necessarily its length, but rather the way many sections feel artificially stretched to reach such numbers.

The pacing is inconsistent, with entire hours of gameplay where the plot barely advances, only to have the entire storyline suddenly shift in specific moments, feeling like a vehicle accelerating and braking so hard it makes your back ache.

While Red Dead Redemption 2's story is roughly the same duration, Arthur Morgan's tale flows smoothly (let's forget about Guarma), and Jason and Lucia's, perhaps intentionally, suffer numerous ups and downs that disconnect you at times.

Grand Theft Auto 6 puts a large emphasis on keeping your relationship sound, so you need to know what ways are the best to raise the romance between Jason and Lucia.

Given GTA 6's size and complexity, the existence of bugs was entirely predictable, and it's rather surprising that, given the hardware, it doesn't include even more technical issues that hinder the player experience.

However, their presence occasionally transcends the anecdotal, with absurdly inconsistent autosaves that cause you to lose hours of progress, permanent weather conditions that don't change, NPCs that appear and disappear, and crashes that shut down the game without warning.

These are just what I've experienced firsthand, but reading anecdotes and watching footage shared online, it's clear that the plethora of errors is much greater, ranging from merely annoying to downright game-breaking.

It's light-years away from being like Cyberpunk 2077's launch, so the comparison is grossly unfair, but the fact that it's been a launch with irregularities is obvious and immediately apparent as soon as you start the game.

I admire the calm with which Rockstar chose to introduce us to the most anticipated video game in history, offering a prologue that, beyond mere formalities, actually extends to the end of Chapter 1.

The entire campaign, both narratively and in terms of gameplay, doesn't truly unfold until after 10 hours, during which you spend more time performing mundane tasks than interacting with GTA 6's rich systems.

Until then, the activities and objectives are quite limited, with few shootouts, no interactions with the police, minimal need for customization, and moderate interactions that only experience occasional bursts of intensity.

While I find this approach daring by AAA standards and think it's commendable, I believe that Colter in Red Dead Redemption 2 also has a slow start, yet with a far superior pace and impact, showing there's room for improvement.

As a result, since GTA 6 inherits its entire exoskeleton from Rockstar's latest release, I have no choice but to compare them directly, and it becomes clear which of the two does a better job of immersing the player in their first hours of gameplay.

This is a brief guide that entails the location of the Fast and Furious green Eclipse in GTA 6.

Since the studio hasn't lost its knack, understandable but erratic, for including dialogue in every commute, GTA 6 suffers from the same weakness that has plagued all the company's games for years.

I've lost count of how many times conversations between characters are interrupted because, since they're tied to the distance between two points, it's common to arrive quickly at your destination only to have the exchange end prematurely.

I know they introduced the option to read the conversation history from the pause menu, but for Rockstar to offer this as their solution to such a long-standing and annoying problem seems truly poor.

It might sound nitpicky, though it breaks the immersion and makes you miss parts of the plot and the relationships between characters, so it's not appropriate to underestimate the issue's magnitude.

Speaking of perpetuating past transgressions, it's surprising how the morality system is an idea replicated ad nauseam in the video game industry, yet virtually no one can implement it successfully.

In this case, you again have a spectrum that oscillates between being a saint or a devil based on specific actions that feel terribly gamified rather than immersive, as they're more of a checklist of behaviors and actions than a genuine human scale.

That petting a cat has a positive impact, just as robbing a drug caravan by only shooting dozens of thugs in the knees is an interesting way to approach the ethical behavior of our protagonists, who will still canonically steal and murder no matter how hard you try to be good.

It's an arbitrary and artificial metric, and while it's partially redeemed by being a measure of criminal professionalism rather than civic morality, it's difficult to reconcile such a realistic and captivating world with a system of emojis that determine your worth as a criminal.

Even just having the system work behind the scenes in accordance with our natural inclinations, like Dishonored, without forcing any kind of action but allowing us to discover the consequences of our moves organically, would be much better, so it feels like a missed opportunity.

Some players may think they should register a hot new sports car as their starter car. There's actually a better choice. Here's the best starter car to register in GTA VI.

Video games find in technology the key to their existence, as it's the mechanism that allows interaction and, therefore, gives meaning to these magical digital worlds in which we can completely blend ourselves.

Consequently, the fact that GTA 6 is the most impressive technical feat we've seen in the industry is enough to consider it revolutionary, yet it deeply troubles me that this capability is used to enhance realism rather than gameplay.

When I'm allowed to perform an action in a title that only tells me how incredibly well-programmed it is, instead of said action serving a purpose within the thematic and gameplay loop its title proposes, it's just empty boasting.

Exercising, grocery shopping, refueling, or eating food are impressive in how they're animated and integrated, though none of them truly contribute to the overall gameplay experience that GTA aims to offer; they could disappear, and it would be completely unnoticeable.

Certainly, there's no such thing as necessary or unnecessary in art, so realism for its own sake also has its place. Regardless, I can't help but think that it slows everything down, and as the hours pass, it distracts you, even if only for a few seconds, from the truly captivating things hidden within the state of Leonida.

Like many games, Grand Theft Auto 6 is full of easter eggs for you to discover. These are some of the best Leonida has to offer.

#4172. Grand Theft Auto VI Review - Outrageous Fortune

Many superlatives will be heard in the discussion around Grand Theft Auto VI – biggest world, most activities, best graphics, deepest narrative – but its real triumph is the way all those features and others work in service of a cohesive, believable immersion in a criminal fantasy that is hard to grasp until you’ve played it for yourself.

Rockstar’s latest returns players to a dramatically expanded version of the Vice City seen in a prior game, now largely unrecognizable after real and in-game years have passed. Leonida is a joy to explore, filled with a wealth of activities, both mundane and illicit. The game’s design makes many ordinary tasks as compelling as the illegal ones. Go fishing off the boat, brew coffee to wake up, work out at the gym, scuba dive for long-lost treasure, dust crops, motocross in the mud, go dancing at the club. As you move between those activities, the world feels alive with minor events, from traffic accidents to shady individuals a little too interested in your walk to the ATM. GTAVI delights in life's minutiae, with animations, voice lines, and background characters that keep things fresh even dozens of hours into the story. The level of detail everywhere is astounding and, at times, overwhelming. Getting sidetracked is easy.

The focus on detail carries into the visuals. Lucia’s hair blows in the wind, and she absently pushes it back behind her ear. A drug den is littered with paraphernalia and empty containers. A shifty contact quirks a smile – your only hint that things are about to go south. Sweat glistens on your character’s skin after a hard workout, their breathing and heart rate noticeably heightened. Clouds roll together in the sky, creating realistic weather simulations. The commitment to an authentic simulated world is encompassing, thoughtful, and intentional, a testament to hand-crafted and meticulously painstaking development work, paying off in an absorbing play-space that is hard to step away from.

While the day-to-day simulation is fascinating, it also adds pacing and counterpoint to the explosive march of major missions, narrative threads, and set-piece encounters that drive the game forward. Not even one of these meticulously choreographed sequences deserves to be spoiled; they run the gamut from amusing shenanigans at a strip club to intense chases and escapes fueled by raging gunfights and explosions. Many of the best moments leverage an expert sense of musical accompaniment, weaving a slick original score alongside one of the most impressive and wide-ranging licensed soundtracks ever heard in a video game – often to surprisingly emotional effect.

Ranged combat is punchy and enjoyable; smart use of cover and time-slowing focus makes most battles manageable. On-foot navigation is in a similar boat – simple to pick up and uninterested in needless complexity or challenge; the focus is on choosing smart moments for stealth, knowing when to run and when to fight, and selecting the precise instant for a burst of sudden action. Driving is fast and intense, made more appealing by a huge variety of functionally distinct vehicles to enjoy. If there’s a fault to the core and optional story missions, it’s that many feel a bit on rails regarding where to go and what to do at each step. At the same time, that directed approach keeps the pace relentless, and the action and outcomes thrilling. Over many hours, the game morphs and throws new wrenches into the mix at key junctures, teasing and then playing out criminal experiences from petty theft to group heists to illicit spec ops, and punctuates those distinct vibes with memorable and singular moments.

Like its predecessors, GTAVI simultaneously lampoons and celebrates life in modern America, taking aim at targets like social media, wellness lifestyles, rap and music culture, manosphere content, and dozens more. The caricatures land so well because, in many cases, they’re (sadly) barely over the line of the absurdity we see reflected in real life, and because Rockstar so ably captures individual subcultures, dialects, and situations. Behind it all is a scathing critique of wealth inequality and the inherent unfairness of a system that sets most up to fail. It’s a bitter message delivered in honey-wrapped, exhilarating gameplay, but it shines through.

Of all its significant feats, the relationship between Lucia and Jason elevates the game to new heights, lending this installment a heart, tension, and emotional core missing from prior entries. This is, without a doubt, video gaming’s most richly drawn and compelling romance, featuring two leads who are immediately relatable and compelling to watch. Player actions dictate the strength of their bond, deepening the sense of engagement. Like the best crime fiction, you’re left surprised by how much you cheer for two people who regularly commit terrible acts. The two collectively suffer the slings and arrows of a world that always seems stacked against them; the fortune they amass is not a power grab, but a desperate attempt to cling to each other and come out the other side together, and the player can’t help but cheer them on and dread how fate might stand in the way.

Grand Theft Auto VI is a generational game that stands toe-to-toe with many of the great crime stories and satires across other media. It showcases both the entertainment value of interactive play and the current high-water mark for technical and artistic detail in games. Hunt for and count up all the minor faults or foibles you like, but then note how you just spent another hour lost in this remarkable escape into criminality, wanton violence, egregious sex, and the elusive potential of true love.

Alex Van Aken contributed to this article.

#4171. Diablo 4’s next class is the Warlock, but you can sort of play it today in Diablo 2: Resurrected’s new DLC

Blizzard has officially unveiled the Warlock, the second class coming to Diablo 4 with Lord of Hatred.

Diablo 4’s segment in the big Diablo 30th Anniversary Spotlight was among the biggest, even if the reason most of us tuned in was somewhat spoiled earlier in the same livestream. Blizzard unveiled the Warlock, the second of two classes coming to the game with the upcoming Lord of Hatred expansion.

The first class, being the Paladin, is already available to play for anyone who pre-ordered the expansion, but the Warlock won’t be accessible until the expansion arrives in late April.

The Warlocks are positioned as the opposite of the Paladins, in that they don’t mind utilising forbidden knowledge, drawing on the powers of Hell itself to fight its own overlords. The Warlock is the edgy, antihero counterpart to the Paladin’s purity and devotion to the Light.

The livestream did not show off any Warlock gameplay, but Blizzard is planning a dedicated livestream to show off the new class’ gameplay, and dig deeper into its lore and abilities. That show is scheduled for March 5.

What we did get to see was our first look at Skovos, the expansion’s new region. This Mediterranean-inspired location is where the new story arc will unfold, but it’s also being positioned as the endgame destination for Diablo 4 once the credits roll.

Lord of Hatred, of course, as previously revealed, introduces two new endgame modes in War Plans, and Echoing Hatred.

War Plans lets you create a custom playlist of up to five endgame activities to target specific rewards and create your own experience. There’s a new activity tree that works with all endgame activities, and creating War Plans is how you earn progression there.

Echoing Hatred, on the other hand, is a rare event that pits you against legions of Mephisto’s minions. It’s triggered through a rare lootable item that unlocks access. It’s essentially horde mode; where you’ll face unending waves of enemies, though not without a couple of twists.

We also got a bit more colour on the expanded class skill trees, which all players will benefit from when the expansion arrives. The Talisman system, which unlocks set bonuses, was also shown off. And, of course, the return of the iconic Horadric Cube, which gives you control over Affixes.

The Anniversary Spotlight should’ve had a Year of the Warlock subtitle, because the class is also making its way to both Diablo Immortal, as well as Diablo 2: Resurrected. The showcase revealed the Reign of the Warlock DLC, which adds the aforementioned Warlock to D2R - its first new class in 25 years.

Reign of the Warlock, which is available now in D2R, also makes a few updates to the game, such as new quality of life features, the Colossal Ancients endgame encounter, updated Terror Zones and more. You also get some cosmetics in Diablo 4 if you purchase this expansion.

The London club’s new duelist is a player who hurt them badly in 2026. Colin ‘CoJo’ Johnson is listed as manager of the rebuilt roster.

The move still has one step left. Pley.gg listed the signing as still awaiting approval from Riot Games. The link is not new. Word of a verbal agreement between marteen and Fnatic emerged on 24 September. That was about a month before Gentle Mates released their whole roster.

Fnatic have already seen what the duelist can do. Gentle Mates came out on top when the two sides met at the 2026 EMEA Kickoff. That win sent Gentle Mates to Masters Santiago.

He led several stat categories in Santiago. Gentle Mates still went out 1–2 to AG and finished joint seventh to eighth. That result earned the team $35,000.

The rest of Gentle Mates’ year was quieter. The team failed to qualify for Masters London or Champions Shanghai. Marteen still finished VCT EMEA Stage 2 as the team’s top-rated player, with a rating of 1.23. Signing a player who stood out in a non-qualifying side suggests Fnatic are building around individual firepower.

Fnatic’s own 2026 campaign ended earlier than planned. Joblife knocked them out with a 2–0 win in the VCT EMEA Stage 2 Play-Ins.

The signing follows a clear-out of long-serving players. Boaster had been with Fnatic since 3 February 2021. Alfajer arrived on 9 May 2022, and crashies on 11 December 2024.

Marteen’s own spell at Gentle Mates ran from 20 November 2025 to 25 October 2026. The two rosters are now tied together by the same transfer window.

Gentle Mates had already cleared their own decks. All five players on the active roster and both coaches were let go before the club’s first season as a VCT partner team.

For a British organisation, the swap leaves Fnatic’s identity in new hands. Boaster had been the longest-serving name in the departing group. Kaajak and Cloud are now the continuity, with marteen as the headline addition.

Welcome to FNATIC, @imthemarteen 🧡 https://t.co/4CxA4zrUDM pic.twitter.com/Tv5CYPQDey

Fnatic do not need to qualify for the opening event. The club is one of eight EMEA partner teams for 2027, and each partner goes straight into Kickoff. Places at later events must be earned. Four teams from Open Qualifiers complete the field.

The first chance to see both rebuilt sides comes soon. The 2027 EMEA Kickoff, featuring 12 teams, runs from 14 January to 7 February 2027 at the Riot Games Arena in Berlin. Its top three teams will qualify for Masters Seoul, the first international event of the 2027 season.

#4167. GTA 6: Complete Beginner's Guide

Usama Mehmood is a Senior Writer at DualShockers with more than five years of experience in the video game industry. He has been writing professionally since 2021 and covering games since 2022, with work spanning guides, lists, reviews, and features across action-adventure games, JRPGs, open-world titles, racing games,

Pretty sure we’ve all had an eventful week with Grand Theft Auto 6 so far because it is undoubtedly the most ambitious video game release, shattering an entertainment-product record on release and going way beyond people’s expectations with the amount of detail and what it has in store. And undeniably, anyone jumping in for the first time may feel overwhelmed by the mechanics and additions.

Grand Theft Auto 6 delivers an enormous open world, a gripping story, a vibrant Vice City and an astonishing range of activities.

But hey, whether you’re a seasoned veteran of the series or totally new to video games who’s playing this blindly for the first time, you don’t have to worry because I've put together an extensive Beginner’s Guide to GTA 6 that compiles the most helpful tips and explanations of the game’s most complex aspects. Strap in, because this will be worth your time, trust.

I’m getting the formalities out of the way first because I’m quickly going to suggest tuning some settings right from the main menu or even in-game, actually. These are all up to you, but I’m mostly here to show you how each one can be helpful.

First, if you’re used to the OG controls of the GTA series, quickly set the control scheme to Classic, as this brings back some familiar GTA 5-style inputs. By default, running and sprinting are mapped to clicking L3, while jumping is assigned to X (A on Xbox). Switching to Classic moves running and sprinting back to X (A), puts crouching on L3, and swaps a few other actions around. I genuinely find it much more comfortable, especially if you've spent years playing the older games.

Next, I'd recommend setting your Minimap to Always On under UI > Navigation. GTA 6's default Dynamic HUD can hide certain information when you're exploring, which looks great for immersion but isn't always practical when you're still learning your way around Leonida. And while you’re at it, reduce Motion Blur Strength if you don’t want to get sick.

And beyond whichever aiming sensitivity suits you, be sure to experiment with the Targeting settings under Gameplay > Combat. Partial is a good middle ground for newcomers, as it helps move your aim towards nearby targets without completely locking onto them. Finally, in UI > Units of Measurement, you can choose your preferred unit system, like the 12-hour clock over the 24-hour one.

Grand Theft Auto 6 puts a large emphasis on keeping your relationship sound, so you need to know what ways are the best to raise the romance between Jason and Lucia.

Briefly going over this as well, since you can easily handle this, contrary to what other players might have you believe. Jason and Lucia are your own, like the little make-believe babies for a class project. Besides their relationship, keep in mind that these characters now have individual stats, like hunger, muscle mass, weight, and sleep management. These can actively influence gameplay in a few ways, such as sleep affecting your total stamina. Meanwhile, things like weight affect how fast you can sprint.

We already have a list of the best ways to boost the couple’s relationship, but the basic gist that you need to remember is not to let them drop to Partners in Crime or below. There are plenty of things that can help you easily boost their relationship, so it’s honestly impossible to not maintain it unless you’re purposely not using both characters or sabotaging it yourself.

And since we’re here, make sure to actively invest in the couple’s BuckMe Family Savings account later on until you max it out at the highest tier, since both that and their relationship are among the primary factors influencing the ending of GTA 6.

Again, you’re free to check our dedicated guide on the mechanic as well, but with the Criminal Profile system, just think of it as a more approachable karma system, like the Honor one from Red Dead 2. This is also one of the other parameters that can influence GTA 6’s ending. A lot of people will have you believe that it strips away your maniacal “GTA” playstyle, but trust me, with everything in your power, this is the most forgiving and manipulable mechanic in the game.

The only thing to watch out for is taking things to the “Irredeemable” state because by that point you can’t revert it back, and you’ll be stuck with that profile unless you have a save file. You can achieve and maintain a Professional Criminal Profile by simply being a good citizen or trying to have as few casualties as possible during side activities, or even successfully making clean getaways and stealth takedowns.

Don’t be afraid to take headshots when necessary because even if you reach a state like Psycho, you can easily change that back by petting a couple of domestic animals, spending some casual time with each other, or just by avoiding headshots altogether for the next few kills by shooting in the limbs instead.

GTA 6 has a noticeably more complex Wanted System than its predecessors. For starters, we’re back to six Wanted Stars, and the police are now much more observant of our actions. Witnesses can report your crimes, security cameras can capture your current identity, and even certain high-end vehicles have trackers that forbid you from just stealing them. In other words, no more crazy Grand Theft Auto-ing.

The biggest change, however, is the introduction of the Heat system. Even after you've managed to lose the cops, they will still remember certain identifying details about you, including your appearance, clothing, getaway vehicle, visible weapons, and whether Jason and Lucia were together. These are represented by small red icons underneath your Wanted Stars, so pay attention to them whenever you're trying to escape.

It’s either how fast you can clear the heat markers off of you in the natural way or some creative tactics that I can suggest, like using water vehicles or boats for escaping higher-level wanted stars, since the rivers and sea tend to be open and less swamped with traffic than VC’s urban infrastructure.

Money plays a much bigger role in GTA 6 than you might initially expect, and you'll quickly find yourself needing extra cash to purchase weapons, clothing for both characters, vehicle upgrades, and other necessities. Thankfully, Leonida is practically overflowing with opportunities to make a quick buck. But the progression works steadily throughout each chapter here.

You’ll start off small by robbing convenience stores and other local businesses in chapter 2, but by chapters 3 and 4, the Robberies tab on your map will be almost flooded with bigger opportunities, including pawn shops, jewelry stores, and banks. Even the occasional gang hideout has different valuables like unique guns to own, vehicles to sell, or safes to bust open and loot.

However, be mindful that robbing a place blind isn't always the smartest idea since many of these sites have security cameras and alarms. Try to use Focus Mode as much as possible to identify enemies, valuable items, and locate safe combinations before making your escape.

Of course, not everything in Leonida requires you to point a gun at someone. There are several side activities that can help you earn some extra money, including stealing vehicles for buyers like Moses and Randy, hunting wildlife for Bret, and competing in Demolition Derbies at Ambrosia Raceway.

One final thing worth remembering is that GTA 6 has three forms of allowance: pocket cash, bank savings, and the valuables you carry in your stash bag. While your bank balance is safe, getting Wasted or Busted can cost you the cash you're carrying, along with any stolen goods you haven't managed to sell, so make a habit of visiting ATMs to deposit your earnings into BuckMe whenever possible.

Many of us are already feeling nostalgic about GTA 6’s first chapter; I mean, seriously, the vibe in Key Lento is unparalleled, especially when playing the game for the first time. But as all things come and go, the vibe doesn't last for long here.

There are a handful of missables you can easily overlook if you rush through the story, so I'd strongly recommend taking your time and exploring everything the Keys have to offer before moving on. Without spoiling, The Tourist Trap mission marks the point of no return for Chapter 1's free roam, so make sure you’re fully ready.

For starters, make sure you complete Shirley's optional jobs, Get Shirley's Rum and Steal the Scooter, as these are exclusive to the first chapter. You might also want to check the loose floorboards for any money you've stashed away, and deposit that into your BuckMe Family Savings.

Lastly, it doesn’t hurt to have a separate manual save for this chapter specifically since GTA 6 doesn't currently let you replay completed story missions, so having a backup gives you the opportunity to revisit Key Lento without having to start another playthrough.

You don't necessarily need to complete every single activity before moving on, but I'd hate for you to miss out on some of the more interesting encounters and neat discoveries Rockstar’s tucked away in this opening chapter. Trust me, you'll appreciate this thing the most here.

Grand Theft Auto 6 makes you lose everything at the end of the first chapter, so make sure that you complete these necessary tasks before taking the plunge into chapter two.

#4166. You're not crazy, trying to heal in Nioh 3 sometimes doesn't work - and Team Ninja is fixing it

One of the more insidiously aggravating bugs in Nioh 3 makes it so the game ignores you when you try to use elixirs, but hopefully not for long.

Nioh 3 has received a hot new update that brings plenty of bug fixes to very specific issues, but it also implements fixes for a few of the most common - and incredibly annoying - bugs. Patch 1.03.01 arrived earlier on all platforms, and it comes with a chunky set of notes.

This latest update, predictably, doesn’t add any gameplay features, but some of the included fixes will absolutely delight - or vindicate - so many of the game’s millions of players.

There’s plenty to go through in the patch notes published today for update 1.03.01, but the most impactful is a fix for an issue that “sometimes made it impossible to use elixirs during battle.” This is only a partial fix, but if you ran into the problem of smashing that shortcut button and not seeing your character play the healing animation, you’ll be glad to see it.

This is a problem myself and others have faced, especially in boss fights. You can even see the shortcut register your button press and proceed to ignore you. Another partial fix has been made to an issue that caused the game to crash. Team Ninja didn’t share specifics on that, and though Nioh 3 has been fairly stable for me in 70+ hours, it has definitely crashed a few times.

If you’ve been playing since launch, you likely have - or know someone who has - run into issues with save file corruption and other weird bugs around certain trackable items within save files.

Team Ninja already rolled out a couple of fixes there, and this latest one specifically targets losing valuables during Myths. If your save file has been affected, the game will now check and recover what was lost. Even more interesting is that the game will now automatically create a backup copy of your save data any time you load a save.

If you’ve made it into the Eternal Rift, you’ll be happy to know that today’s update takes care of a few progression blockers, and fixes an issue that allowed some players to obtain certain items before they were supposed to, locking themselves out.

One of the more amusing fixes concerns Mujina, who had a tendency to respawn if you prayed at a Shrine after opening a chest it was hiding in, which made it appear far more often than a mimic should.

Finally, there’s a set of fixes that address bugs (and exploits) when using specific Martial Art with certain weapons. There are a few fixes to AI, Myths, and one problem with the Minamoto no Yoritomo boss fight that made it impossible to interrupt him, even after he runs out of Ki.

Hit the link at the top for the full change log, and check out our Nioh 3 gameplay tips if you haven’t already. You should also change these settings ASAP, as they’re going to make your life much easier and save you a lot of time.
