#4165. FaZe crash out of PGL Major Singapore in Stage 1 as HEROIC beat them again 11 days on

HEROIC have sent FaZe Clan home from the PGL Major Singapore 2026 before Stage 2. A side that reached a Major final in 2024 now faces questions about its roster heading into 2027, with captain Twistzz admitting the team has gone backwards.

Rio 2022 was the last time FaZe Clan fared worse at a Major.

The campaign started badly. FaZe opened on 24 November with a 9-13 best-of-one defeat to Wildcard, Dot Esports reported. Their only win in Singapore came that same day, a comfortable result against BC.Game on Mirage. PARIVISION then beat them 13-10 on 25 November. That defeat dropped FaZe into the 1-2 elimination pool, where HEROIC were waiting.

Singapore marked the second time in under two weeks that HEROIC ended a FaZe campaign. Mirage and Ancient had decided the earlier sweep. FaZe had won the meeting before that, knocking HEROIC out of DraculaN in October. HEROIC have now won the two most recent encounters, both with elimination at stake.

The roster has changed shape this year. Under karrigan, the organisation won its first Major title. FaZe then missed the IEM Cologne 2026 Major, and karrigan left for Team Falcons.

Twistzz took over as in-game leader. The early signs were encouraging. FaZe finished in the top four at XSE Pro League Guangzhou and BLAST Bounty Season 2. Results then fell away. The team failed to get beyond the top 16 at the Esports World Cup, FISSURE Playground 3 and IEM Beijing.

Twistzz was frank on PGL’s broadcast after the defeat. He said FaZe had “regressed a lot as a team” over the season, and perhaps individually too. He also described himself as not the most experienced captain. In his view, he does his best work with a second voice to bounce ideas off. That points to a structural question for the side, not just a bad week in Singapore.

The decline is stark against recent history. FaZe reached the final of the Perfect World Shanghai Major 2024. Spirit beat them there to take the title and US$500,000, leaving FaZe with US$170,000.

Twistzz had some strong words after FaZe's Singapore Major Elimination ‼️

"Honestly, I wish I could be more frustrated… but the reality of the situation is that we were not a team that felt extremely competitive before coming to this event.

FaZe is like a big name, but… pic.twitter.com/7mpHCtxiB4

PGL announced the event as the second CS2 Major of 2026 and the first Counter-Strike 2 Major in Southeast Asia. It carries a US$1,250,000 prize pool. The tournament runs from 24 November to 13 December with 32 teams.

HEROIC play Lynn Vision on 27 November for one of the last three places in Stage 2. The playoffs follow from 10 to 13 December at the Singapore Indoor Stadium, which holds more than 12,000 people.

#4164. We Got These 102 Things Before GTA VI

Grand Theft Auto VI is here. Let’s pat ourselves on the back; we made it. While it's a day of jubilation for many, it’s also a day of mourning as we’re losing an important piece of our cultural fabric: the “We got ________ before GTA VI” meme.

The meme is officially retired, so let’s remember it by looking back at a random assortment of memorable and, in many cases, unlikely events, in no particular order, that did indeed occur during the 13-year wait between GTA V and GTA VI.

#4163. Genshin Impact Luna 5 takes the squad back to Mondstadt, finally makes Varka playable

Genshin Impact's next update will have you reminiscing about the good ol' days of... 2020.

The latest big content update has been revealed for HoYoverse's breakout game, Genshin Impact. Version Luna 5, which has the unusually long and needlessly layered title — Song of the Welkin Moon: Variation - Homeward, He Who Caught the Wind — is set to arrive February 25.

This one is a bit of a nostalgia play, taking everyone back to Mondstadt, the place where you may remember taking your first steps. And, as with any good return to the ol’ hunting grounds, come familiar characters, too.

The big new arrival is Varka, who joins as a playable character for the first time. Varka, Grand Master of the Knights of Favonius, is a character whose debut has been long-awaited. He is a 5-Star Anemo Claymore wielder with a dual-wield combat style, capable of dealing two different types of Elemental damage. His addition means that there's now finally a burly 5-Star male character of each elemental type... do with that information what you will.

Varka's dual-wielding combat style allows him to deal two different types of Elemental damage at the same time. The way it works is that his Elemental Skill boosts the damage of his regular attacks, but it also converts the damage type of his right-hand claymore to match his teammates’ elements (Pyro, Hydro, Electro, or Cryo). The left-hand claymore always deals Anemo damage.

The more normal attacks you use, the more frequently he can activate a special Elemental Skill, or trigger a Charged Attack that doesn’t consume stamina. He can also rely on the Hexerei effect to trigger more instances of Elemental Skill, as well as Charged Attacks, making him a monster damage-dealer.

Varka, of course, has been a staple member of the cast, featuring in both the original story in a small cameo, as well as taking a bigger role in the recent Nod-Krai chapters. With the return to Mondstadt, his playable debut makes sense. His Story Quest will shed light on his encounter with the Wild Hunt, and the Great Wolf King of the North

The reruns for this version are going to be Flins — who will be available in the first phase of Event Wishes — as well as Skirk and Escoffier in the second phase. You can also look forward to the return of the Chronicled Wish with Mondstadt characters.

Staying on the theme of reminiscence, the big event in Luna 5 is centered around revisiting memories from the beginning of your time with Genshin Impact, and reuniting with old friends. In Echoes of Memory, you’ll witness familiar scenes that have been changed slightly, and you’ll need to use the Spotter Kamera to detect and record those differences.

The Knights of Favonius are hosting several other activities for everyone to take part in, including an event that lets you catch up with old friends over drinks which you make for them.

Outside of events, there’s a new set of Gliding and Combat Challenges. And, of course, there are new minigames that you can relax with. The Kamera is being utilised yet again, and this time you can use to capture sights from your time in spots across Natlan, Fontaine, and Sumeru. There’s also… a horde mode of a sort, where you fend off waves of enemies.

#4162. PUBG Mobile’s music project The Squad kicks off with IVE's Renegade

Krafton has a new music project on the go called The Squad, and K-pop group IVE is the first act involved. It spans both PUBG: Battlegrounds and PUBG Mobile, so this time those of you on iOS and Android get in on it as well, with collab content heading to mobile in December.

IVE was already in Battlegrounds earlier this month. That was the Love Dive collab, which brought themed content to Rondo along with some character items and cosmetics, and it was a fairly soft, pretty sort of affair.

The new song, Renegade, is supposed to go the other way and be a lot bolder. You can judge for yourself on December 2nd when the full music video comes out or have a look at the teaser that's already up on PUBG's channels.

Going forward, Krafton wants a run of different artists to each make an original song inspired by PUBG, and every one of them gets their own themed stuff in the games off the back of it. More are on the way after IVE, apparently, which ties in with PUBG's tenth anniversary coming up in 2027.

As for when it all lands, PC is first on December 2nd and PUBG Mobile gets it on December 7th, then console on the 10th. PC and console get themed locations to drop into too. Mobile isn't mentioned for those, so it's items only for now, as far as I can see.

That's a bit of a shame for mobile. Mobile fans have been asking for an IVE crossover all year, and PUBG Mobile has done a whole string of celebrity collabs in 2026. Getting it five days after PC and without the new locations makes mobile feel like a bit of an afterthought here. It's still a nice haul of cosmetics if you're a fan, though.

While you wait, have a look at our list of the best battle royale games on Android.
